text:
maria: Heads up — seeing intermittent packet loss (~0.5-2%) inside the overlay when we scale GPU pools in us-west. Jobs hit stalls, retries spike, and some gRPC streams drop. Noticed it after last k8s autoscaler bump.
aj: Can you paste the pod->pod ping/iperf? Is this VXLAN or Geneve?
maria: Geneve on most nodes in that cluster. Quick iperf3 from gpu-pod-a -> gpu-pod-b (same node and cross-node):
```
# same-node
iperf3 -c 10.0.3.22 -t 20
[SUM]   20.00 sec   9.12 GBytes  3.92 Gbits/sec
# cross-node
iperf3 -c 10.0.4.11 -t 20
[SUM]   20.00 sec   6.58 GBytes  2.83 Gbits/sec
```
latency spikes visible in tcpdump: some retransmits and RTOs during brief bursts.
kevin: Any MTU mismatches? Also check offloads: GSO/TSO/GRO can misbehave with encap.
maria: MTU is 1450 cluster-wide (encap overhead). I ran `ip -s link show vxlan0` and saw rx errors bump during scale events: 
```
3: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc pfifo_fast state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    RX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped overrun mcast
    123456789  98765    12      4       0       0
    TX: bytes  packets  errors  dropped carrier collsns
    987654321  123456   0       8       0       0
```
aj: Dropped TX on vxlan is suspicious. Are these nodes using different NIC drivers/firmware? We saw similar with intel+mlx5 heterogeneity before.
kevin: I also want to see `ethtool -k` and `dmesg` for the NICs. Could be offload + encap corner. Firmware mismatch causes ring drops under burst.
elaine: infra-bot pulled recent node metadata: 6 nodes in this AZ are on kernel 5.15 + mlx5 5.12 driver, rest on 6.1 + mlx5 5.15. Autoscaler tends to schedule new GPU pods on older nodes first due to binpacking.
infra-bot: [node-metadata] node-7: NIC=mlx5_core v5.12 fw=12.8, node-12: NIC=mlx5_core v5.15 fw=14.1, kubelet=1.24, mtu=1450
maria: Reproduced with a small churn test: scale GPU daemonset from 0->10 quickly. Packet drops coincide with pod creation spikes.
aj: Can you try disabling GSO on vxlan for a short run? Quick command on host: `ethtool -K vxlan0 gso off gro off tso off` and retest. If that stabilizes, it's likely offload/encap bug.
maria: Done on 2 nodes, reran iperf during scale: cross-node bandwidth now steady ~3.9 Gbits, no rx errors in `ip -s link`. Initial short test looks promising :thumbsup:
kevin: If that fixes, we should push a node-level daemon to toggle offloads for vxlan on affected NIC+driver combos until firmware/driver patch available. Also open vendor ticket for firmware regression.
elaine: Cost/ops note — turning off offloads increases CPU overhead on high-throughput nodes. Need to measure impact on utilization for dedicated GPU workloads.
aj: Add a canary to autoscaler so new pods avoid old-driver nodes until we have fix. Also plan a rolling fw upgrade for the cluster fleet in that AZ.
maria: Filed a quick incident note and linked the test logs: https://redwood-internal/infra/INC-2026-243 (summary + iperf dumps + tcpdump snippets).
kevin: I'll open a vendor ticket with mlx5 logs and dmesg, include repro steps (fast pod churn + geneve MTU 1450 + GSO on).
elaine: Action items:
- kevin: vendor ticket + logs (ETA today)
- aj: rollout autoscaler canary and taint old-driver nodes (ETA 2h)
- maria: run CPU impact baseline with offloads disabled (ETA tomorrow)
- infra: schedule firmware upgrades in us-west pool (planning next week)

maria: Thanks — will monitor and report back. :eyes:
